The learner asks specifically: Make sure one of the senses is this meaning: a word that joins two contrasting ideas.

notes: When used at the start of a sentence, 'demo' acts as a conjunction meaning 'but' or 'however', linking a previous statement with a contrasting one.
When used after a noun, it functions as a particle meaning 'even' or 'also' (e.g., 'kodomo demo dekiru' - 'even a child can do it').
It is a very common word in daily conversation. If you want to be more formal in writing, use 'shikashi' instead.

senses.definition: Used at the beginning of a sentence to connect two contrasting thoughts.

examples.text: 明日は忙しいです。でも、行きます。
examples.translation: Tomorrow is busy. But, I will go.

senses.definition: Used after a word to mean 'even' or 'at least'.
